daily.title: Bus, train collide, injuring 19 at Channel Tunnel terminal
daily.summary: A minibus carrying truck drivers collided with a freight train near the Channel Tunnel entrance in France, injuring 19 people, with five severely hurt. Emergency services rushed to the scene.

daily.title: Venezuela's Nicolas Maduro pleads not guilty to torture charges
daily.summary: Maduro and his wife were charged with leading a state-sponsored repression campaign that tortured scores of victims during his presidency from 2013 to 2026.

daily.title: Self-replicating AI: Is your fridge a cybersecurity risk?
daily.summary: Anthropic researchers warn that AI worms could soon target connected household devices and spread from one device to another. Cyberattacks on French supermarkets illustrate just how vulnerable such systems can be.

daily.title: Middle East updates: Houthis target Yemen government palace in Aden
daily.summary: Houthi rebels say they targeted Saudi military assets in a rare attack on the interim seat of Yemen's internationally recognized government. Meanwhile, vessels are again under fire near the Strait of Hormuz. More on DW.

daily.title: Police raid the major pro-opposition Halk TV channel in Turkey
daily.summary: Turkish police raided the Istanbul headquarters of an important pro-opposition television station on Wednesdazy, the day that jailed Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu was set to start his defense against corruption charges.

daily.title: Trump says execution of Fort Hood shooter will not be livestreamed
daily.summary: Trump said the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan can be viewed in person by families of the victims if they wish. The decision comes after bipartisan backlash regarding the Pentagon's plans to livestream the execution.

daily.title: Russia arrests Swedish national, claims he's Ukraine fighter
daily.summary: Russian intelligence agents have arrested a Swedish man they say led a Ukrainian drone unit. He was detained at Russia's western border and is accused of planning acts of terrorism and sabotage.

daily.title: Ukraine resumes attacks on Russian refineries as Zelenskyy says 'we're done'
daily.summary: Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said Ukraine will again attack Russian energy sites, as Moscow has ignored a claim by US President Trump that an "energy ceasefire" had been agreed. Russia reported two attacks on refineries.

daily.title: Can Kenya preserve the democratic space Raila Odinga fought for?
daily.summary: One year after the former prime minister's death, Kenyans are reflecting on his contribution to democracy and national reconciliation. Odinga's "handshakes" with his political rivals remain the subject of much debate.

daily.title: EU summit to focus on China, Ukraine and bloc budget
daily.summary: EU leaders meeting in Brussels will examine measures to curb the bloc's huge trade deficit with China. But they will also be looking to further agreement on the next EU budget ahead of some major elections next year.

daily.title: Romania: 2 ships on fire in Black Sea, 7 crew missing
daily.summary: Two chemical tankers have caught fire in Romanian territorial waters in the Black Sea. The blazes occurred after Russian drones were sighted in Romanian airspace.

daily.title: Resignation of Bärbel Bas shines light on harsh era of German politics
daily.summary: German Labor Minister Bärbel Bas has stepped down, citing her need to grieve a loved one and leave behind the harsh realities of government. So how did German politics get so heated?

daily.title: Hamburg court jails 2 men over plot to attack Jewish leaders on behalf of Iran
daily.summary: The men were found guilty of espionage and attempted murder. According to the court, they planned to attack the president of the Central Council of Jews in Germany and president of the German-Israeli society.

daily.title: AI-assisted dying? Doris Dörrie's new film addresses prospect of care robots
daily.summary: While the world debates the dangers of artificial intelligence, filmmaker Doris Dörrie explores how humanoid robots could change the way we deal with aging, caregiving and how people choose to die.

daily.title: Starlink: How Elon Musk's company influences geopolitics
daily.summary: Designed to bring internet access to remote regions, Elon Musk's Starlink has become vital in crisis regions and war zones. But Ukraine also shows the risks of depending on the service.

daily.title: Hypersonic missiles highlight arms race on Korean Peninsula
daily.summary: Both South and North Korea have tested weapons feared by military planners for their speed and ability to maneuver in flight.

daily.title: Thousands of German gamblers could sue for their money back
daily.summary: German gamblers may finally be able to beat the house, thanks to new court rulings in the EU and in Germany. The decisions could help gambling addicts — but the legal road might be difficult.

daily.title: School roof collapse in Pakistan's Peshawar kills dozens of students and one teacher
daily.summary: Local authorities said more than 50 other people were injured in the disaster. Roof collapses have become increasingly common in Pakistan.

daily.title: Germany news: Train station alcohol ban comes into force
daily.summary: Consuming alcohol is no longer permitted at train stations in Germany, to improve the lot of travelers and staff alike. Coalition talks are restarting in Berlin, and an inmate is loose in Essen. Follow DW for more.

daily.title: Brazil's elections matter for the planet. This is why
daily.summary: Brazil is heading back to the polls, but the impact could be felt worldwide. With the Amazon vital to the health of the planet, the election could help shape its future.

daily.title: Why Chinese tech brands are outpacing Western rivals from EVs to robot vacuums
daily.summary: From action cameras and smartphones to EVs and robot vacuums, Chinese brands are gaining ground worldwide, despite privacy and security concerns. What's driving their rise, and can European rivals keep up?

daily.title: Manchester City, the UAE and the UK's OM in a political tangle
daily.summary: Nearly 20 years after arriving in England, Manchester City's UAE owners could exit amid cheating charges. That would pose a challenge for a city — and prime minister — closely tied to Abu Dhabi.

weekly.title: Nord Stream trial opens in Germany, defense seeks dismissal
weekly.summary: Serhii Kuznietsov is accused of attacking civilian infrastructure in the 2022 sabotage of the Russian gas pipeline to Germany. His lawyers called Nord Stream a military target, and said their client is sworn to secrecy.

weekly.title: Germany's far-right AfD forges a pro-Russia alliance with the BSW
weekly.summary: In Saxony-Anhalt, the AfD and BSW are joining forces to push for negotiations with Moscow. What is driving this rapprochement?

weekly.title: Albania: Fire at Education Ministry as students protest
weekly.summary: Riot police deployed in the Albanian capital Tirana on the second day of student protests. The sudden outbreak seemed at least somewhat reminiscent of the widespread demos in France courting international attention.

weekly.title: Trump's diesel deal with Russia is unlikely to significantly lower global fuel prices despite expectations of rapid relief
weekly.summary: As the world's largest diesel exporter, the US benefits from high prices. At home, however, consumers are feeling the strain of rising living costs. Why Donald Trump's deal with Russia is unlikely to change that.

weekly.title: China's influence in the gaming industry is growing
weekly.summary: Home to more than 700 million gamers, China is the world's largest gaming market — but it's also one of the most tightly regulated. The effects reach far beyond China, impacting players around the world.

weekly.title: Nord Stream: Germany puts suspected Ukrainian pipeline saboteur on trial
weekly.summary: A Ukrainian citizen faces court in Hamburg, accused of attacking the Nord Stream gas pipelines in 2022. It raises questions about Kyiv's possible role in the explosions. German support for Ukraine is also under scrutiny.

weekly.title: Fact check: Misleading graph about alleged Russian bot activity
weekly.summary: Did attacks on Russian data centers reduce bot activity around Germany's AfD? A viral graph claims they did. But it contains significant inconsistencies and provides no evidence to support the claim.

weekly.title: Do non-German nationals commit more crimes than Germans?
weekly.summary: People without German passports appear more frequently in German police crime statistics than German nationals. A new study explains why.

weekly.title: FIFPRO report highlights growing pains in women's football
weekly.summary: Expected global revenue of over $1 billion and new faces at the U17 World Cup show women's football is booming, but a recent report also highlights need for better structures globally.

weekly.title: The hidden treasure in discarded wearable and fast tech
weekly.summary: Sales of fast tech like mini fans and disposable e-vapes, as well as wearable health tech such as heart monitors and smartwatches are soaring. They're creating a new e-waste problem but are full of hidden treasure.

weekly.title: Ukraine allies in Poland after Starlink sabotage, Trump diesel deal
weekly.summary: Germany's Johann Wadephul said hybrid plots like the Starlink fire showed Europe was "in Russia's crosshairs." The UK's Ed Miliband said Trump's Russian diesel deal led to a "very difficult few days" diplomatically.

weekly.title: Ukraine and the US: What's next after Trump's diesel deal with Russia?
weekly.summary: Donald Trump plans to allow the purchase of Russian diesel, drawing criticism at home and abroad. What is behind the US president's decision and what should Ukraine do next? DW spoke with experts.

weekly.title: Critics warn of espionage risks as Slovakia restores military-diplomatic representation with Russia
weekly.summary: Slovakia is restoring military-diplomatic relations with Russia for the first time since 2022. The government has defended the move but critics warn of espionage risks and further damage to trust within NATO.

weekly.title: Formula 1: Rwanda to bring sport back to Africa
weekly.summary: The last time Formula 1 hosted a race in Africa was way back in 1993. But a new track in Rwanda is set to host a Grand Prix in "the early 2030s," continuing the country’s investment in international sport.

weekly.title: Germany's China calculation shifts as import pressures eclipse export benefits
weekly.summary: Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base.

weekly.title: 125 years of Thomas Mann's 'Buddenbrooks'
weekly.summary: This over 1,000-page masterpiece offers a panoramic view of society in the 19th century and exposes the collapse of a merchant family: unrecognized sons, disillusioned daughters and the loss of middle-class ideals.

weekly.title: What is holding back Cyprus's Schengen ambitions?
weekly.summary: The European Commission says Cyprus is ready to join the Schengen Area. Yet questions relating to the island's division and British military bases could still complicate its path to Europe's border-free travel zone.

weekly.title: UK: Iran 'highly likely' to be behind RAF Fairford incident
weekly.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham told parliament there were "strong indications" of Iranian involvement. The government summoned Iran's ambassador. The scare at RAF Fairford led to the withdrawal of USAF B-1 heavy bombers.

weekly.title: Poland reports arrests of 2 Turkish citizens in Germany in connection with Starlink station fire last month
weekly.summary: Polish authorities have reported the arrests of two Turkish citizens in Germany in connection with alleged sabotage of a Starlink station last month. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the fire an act of "hybrid warfare."

weekly.title: Germany: Labor Minister's resignation puts a spotlight on cracks within the government
weekly.summary: Following the sudden resignation of Bärbel Bas as Labor Minister and co-chair of the Social Democratic Party, accusations are flying in Chancellor Merz's coalition government.

weekly.title: Pope lung nodule: Could it be cancer?
weekly.summary: The case of Pope Leo shows how small lung nodules are often found during routine health checks. Quick treatment is generally advised before nodules can grow to become larger life-threatening masses.

weekly.title: Germany's women: Ena Mahmutovic makes her case to become Germany's next No.1 goalkeeper
weekly.summary: Germany's win against Australia saw Ena Mahmutovic excel in goal. The 22-year-old Bayern Munich goalkeeper is considered the successor to Ann-Katrin Berger and is making a name for herself.

weekly.title: How green is Europe's urban public transport? A data-driven reality check
weekly.summary: Greener buses and cleaner fleets are reshaping public transport across Europe. But are cities moving fast enough to meet their zero-emission goals?

weekly.title: UK students call for school uniforms to be banned in pornography
weekly.summary: Short skirts, knee-high socks, white blouses: Girls' school uniform items are widely used as costumes in pornographic videos. As students experience harassment, a group wants to change that.

weekly.title: Who are the Ukrainian 'volunteers' under Russian command?
weekly.summary: Russia has announced a battalion consisting of Ukrainian "volunteers." But veterans and former prisoners of war share very different accounts.

weekly.title: German 'lawfare': When lawsuits become a political weapon
weekly.summary: The Left Party is suing two government ministers for accusing them of antisemitism, while Chancellor Friedrich Merz has been sued several times by various parties. Is German politics descending into "lawfare?"

weekly.title: Trump claims Russia and Ukraine agreed to 'energy ceasefire'
weekly.summary: US President Donald Trump says both sides have agreed to stop targeting oil refineries, power plants and other energy infrastructure immediately.

weekly.title: Georgia's surrogacy industry is booming, but at what cost?
weekly.summary: Georgia became a hub for surrogate pregnancies after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. DW spoke with parents, and those who wanted to become parents, about the hidden costs of a booming industry.

weekly.title: Germany's population is shrinking, but not everywhere
weekly.summary: By 2045, Germany will have more older people, fewer workers and a smaller population overall. Yet some regions will defy this trend. Their success depends on how much they have to offer.

weekly.title: 'Ragebait' is the 2026 German Youth Word of the Year
weekly.summary: Already named the 2025 Oxford Word of the Year, "rage bait" has also been widely adopted in German slang.

weekly.title: Operations Plan Germany: How the Bundeswehr trains for NATO collective defense
weekly.summary: How prepared is Germany for national defense? The answer lies in the Operations Plan Germany. Military exercises such as "Red Storm Charlie" are designed to put these preparations to the test in realistic scenarios.

weekly.title: Schools crisis in France: Investment fails to inspire confidence
weekly.summary: For weeks, schoolchildren in France have been protesting the failing education system. Compared to many other countries, France invests heavily in education but critics say that the funds are not distributed fairly.

weekly.title: Macron and Steinmeier struggle to revive Franco-German ties
weekly.summary: Presidents Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Emmanuel Macron are about to step down from their offices. Their meeting in France made it clear how urgently the Franco-German partnership needs new momentum.

weekly.title: Author or artificial intelligence? Literature in crisis
weekly.summary: AI is a hot topic at this year's Frankfurt Book Fair. An international literary scandal has raised questions about machine-generated texts.

weekly.title: Art for freedom: Maria Kalesnikava in Bonn
weekly.summary: The Belarusian musician and civil rights activist Maria Kalesnikava held the keynote speech on the importance of art at the 2026 Beethovenfest in Bonn. She also visited DW.

weekly.title: Poland: Lifeline for Ukrainian refugees confronts donor fatigue and online abuse as anti-Ukrainian sentiment grows
weekly.summary: A Ukrainian woman who fled the war in her country built a lifeline for refugees in Poland. Now her organization faces donor fatigue, funding cuts and rising hostility as support for Ukrainians in Poland wanes.

weekly.title: World Cup 2034: Does Saudi Arabia shelving Neom Stadium spell trouble?
weekly.summary: Since winning the right to hold the 2034 World Cup unopposed, Saudi Arabia has been pulling away from sport. With reports that its most ambitious stadium project will be abandoned, what does this mean for the World Cup?

weekly.title: Bosnia-Herzegovina will soon have a new grand mufti
weekly.summary: The new leader of the Islamic Community in Bosnia-Herzegovina will be elected on October 10. The reis-ul-ulema's role is not only important for Muslims in the country itself, but could inspire Muslims across Europe.

weekly.title: Finland, the world's happiest nation, faces a glum winter
weekly.summary: Finns have many reasons to feel content, but the country's pile of debt is not one of them. Russia's war in Ukraine has added to the fiscal burden. Can the Nordic nation absorb another shock?

developing.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
developing.summary: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.
